newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco stadium race too close to call.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco stadium race too close to call.

text.p: San Francisco voters appear to have given their backing to a new $525 million football stadium-mall project in a special election, but city officials said on Wednesday the race was still too close to call.
With all of the voting precincts reporting, the two stadium measures on Tuesday's ballot had approval majorities of several hundred votes each.
"How sweet it is," San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown told supporters celebrating the narrow lead.
San Francisco election officials said, however, thousands of additional ballots still had to be counted, and that it was too soon to declare a winner.

Proposition D authorizes the sale of up to $100 million of bonds to finance the city's share of the proposed San Francisco 49ers football stadium and shopping complex. Proposition F waives zoning restrictions to speed construction.
Stadium opponents had argued that the project was a form of "corporate welfare" because it would put San Francisco's budget on the line for the benefit of wealthy team owners.

Stadium supporters promised that the city would never have to dip into its general fund budget to pay off the bonds, and told voters the project would create thousands of jobs for one of the city's poorest neighborhoods.
